\chapter{Boolean Analysis --- Finite Noise Duality}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.RandomVariables.Sharp.FiniteNoiseDuality
\section{Overview}
The weighted averaging noise operator is self-adjoint and has an explicit second-moment formula. A signed-power dual vector converts its conjugate-exponent contraction into forward hypercontractivity.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{theorem}[Signed-power duality identities]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.SharpDiscrete.signed_power_dual}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
Let $q>2$ and $z\in\mathbb R$, and set $g=z|z|^{q-2}$. Then $zg=|z|^q$ and
$|g|^{q/(q-1)}=|z|^q$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Weighted noise identities]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.SharpDiscrete.finite_noise_identities}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
Let $I$ be a finite set, let $w_i\in\mathbb{R}$ satisfy $\sum_i w_i=1$, and let
$\rho\in\mathbb{R}$ and $f,g:I\to\mathbb{R}$. Write $m_f=\sum_i w_i f_i$ and $m_g=\sum_i
w_i g_i$. Then both identities hold:
\[
\sum_i w_i\bigl(\rho g_i+(1-\rho)m_g\bigr)^2=\rho^2\sum_i w_i g_i^2+(1-\rho^2)m_g^2,
\qquad
\sum_i w_i\bigl(\rho f_i+(1-\rho)m_f\bigr)g_i=\sum_i w_i f_i\bigl(\rho
g_i+(1-\rho)m_g\bigr).
\]
\end{theorem}
